function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) have no posted maximum, but drivers must still obey “reasonable and prudent” speed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Failure to buckle can result in a $50 fine. | Texas Transportation Code §545.002 | | **DUI / DWI** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• First offense: up to 90 days jail, $2,000 fine, 1‑year license suspension.
• Repeat offenders face harsher penalties. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Violations can lead to a $50 fine. | Texas Transportation Code §545.003 | | **Headlights & Signal Use** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Turn signals must be used at least 100 ft before turning. | Texas Transportation Code §545.004 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at red lights, stop signs, and yield signs.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Texas Transportation Code §545.005 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or within 20 ft of a crosswalk.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | Texas Transportation Code §545.006 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Failure to stop can result in a $500 fine. | Texas Transportation Code §545.007 | | **Vehicle Inspection & Registration** | • Annual vehicle inspection required for most vehicles.
• Registration renewal is due annually; late fees apply. | Texas Transportation Code §545.008 | | **Towing & Towage** | • Towing of vehicles requires a valid towing permit.
• Unlawful towing can lead to civil liability. | Texas Transportation Code §545.009 | ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website: [https://www.txdot.gov](https://www.txdot.gov) *Provides current statutes, rule changes, and public notices.* 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Accessible online via the Texas Legislature’s website: [https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/) *Full legal text of all traffic laws.* 3. **Local County Courts** – For specific enforcement actions or court rulings, check your county’s court website. 4. **Legal Aid & Law Firms** – If you’re facing a traffic violation or need legal representation, consult a licensed Texas attorney. --- #### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s the single most effective way to reduce injury. - **Avoid distractions** – hands‑free only, no texting or calling while driving. - **Know your speed limits** – they’re posted on signs; if none, drive at a safe speed for conditions. - **Respect school buses** – stop fully and wait until the bus resumes motion. - **Keep your vehicle in good shape** – regular inspections help avoid fines and keep you safe. Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detailed information on any specific law or if you need help locating a particular statute!
